Maya R: Quick sync request 8min		Heads-up  prep for a compact battlecard refresh vs cloud AI providers and managed LLM APIs. Need minimal rebut bullets and a one-liner for security decks. Can we spin this up by EOD?
Sanjay Patel: +1. We should center on three defensible metrics: P95 latency, steady-state $/1k tokens, and rollback/rollout controls. Which of those is most compelling to call out?
Tess Nguyen: P95 and steady-state cost. Ops validated continuous batching + KV cache savings on Dedicated showing ~32% cost reduction on conversational workloads with long prefixes.
Ben Cho: I'll prepare a tiny cost note. Important: don't say "faster" without model config. Emphasize "predictable latency and tail control".
Marco Li: Procurement wants security soundbites: VPC, customer KMS, and audit logs. Add a 1-liner for decks.
Maya R: Draft one-liner candidate: "Production-first inference: predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private)." Too long?
Tess Nguyen: Shorten: "Predictable latency. Predictable cost. Deploy where you need to." Cleaner.
Sanjay Patel: For the battlecard structure propose: 1) Quick claim vs cloud AI 2) Quick claim vs LLM APIs 3) SDR rebut bullets 4) Demo prompts 5) Watchlist signals.
Ben Cho: Draft rebut for cost: `If a provider shows lower sticker price, ask about long-tail token inflation, cache reuse, and whether they expose prefix reuse capabilities.`
Maya R: SDR script idea: "If asked about managed endpoints, highlight SLA, burst capacity, and kernel-level ops that reduce tail latency."
comp-bot: Benchmark upload: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/2026-03-inference-vs-cloud.csv (verified) :ledger:
Marco Li: Pulled CSV. P95s look consistent on T4/T4p sim. Recommend A/B phrase: "When latency matters, choose dedicated pools; when elasticity matters, choose hosted."
Tess Nguyen: Webinar idea: 30-min demo hitting hosted vs dedicated vs private with identical prompt set. Title: "Serving the Real World: Cost, Latency, and Reliability at Scale". Include 10-min procurement/security Q&A.
Sanjay Patel: Good. Who owns demo infra? @Ben Cho can stand up harness, @Marco Li to vet security config. Ben, can you include SOP for metrics capture?
Ben Cho: Yes. Will include a small harness + metrics SOP and five canonical prompts: short chat, instruction prompt, long context thread, retrieval-augmented completion, code generation.
Maya R: Rebut bullets (short):
- Claim: "Cloud provider X is cheaper."
  Rebuttal: "Unit economics depend on batching and cache reuse; at scale conv workloads see ~30% lower unit cost with our Dedicated profiles."
- Claim: "Managed LLM APIs are simpler."
  Rebuttal: "Good for prototypes. Production requires SLAs, rollout controls, and predictable capacity which Redwood provides."
- Claim: "You can just run on public cloud GPUs."
  Rebuttal: "True, but engineering and ops overhead to get predictable token-level cost and tail latency is non-trivial; Redwood bundles runtime, routing, and monitoring."
Tess Nguyen: Add a 2-line tech footnote for AE decks: mention prefix KV cache, continuous batching, and quantization-friendly execution path as drivers of cost and latency improvements. Keep it non-verbose.
Sanjay Patel: Add procurement table: hosted usage (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), private license + support (license + SOW). Helps procurement triage quickly.
Maya R: Action items: Ben -> demo harness + metrics SOP (due EOD tomorrow). Marco -> security one-pager for procurement (due in 2 days). Tess -> draft battlecard bullets + A/B phrasing (due EOD). Sanjay -> compile benchmark highlights + 2-slide webinar appendix (due tomorrow noon). I'll stitch and send for review.
Ben Cho: On it, will ping infra channel when the harness is up. :thumbsup:
Marco Li: Drafting KMS and VPC pitch now.
Tess Nguyen: Posting battlecard draft in ~45m.
Maya R: Final note: keep competitor mentions categorical ("cloud AI providers", "managed LLM APIs"). We'll keep competitor-specific callouts in a locked doc.
Sanjay Patel: Also include a short checklist for SDRs: 1) ask about their tail latency SLOs 2) ask about prefix reuse 3) ask about procurement restrictions (KMS, audit).
Maya R: Perfect. Meeting set for review in 24h.
